title: Check yourself: The gate, the roll-out and the way back

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A staged roll-out sits at 5 percent of traffic. Only 300 requests have been counted, with no errors, and the minimum is 1,000. What is the next step?

options.text: Advance to 25 percent, since a clean record needs no further evidence
options.says: Ruled out because "A stage with fewer requests than the minimum (1,000 in the example) says nothing yet".

options.text: Hold where it is, since a sample this small shows nothing yet
options.says: A stage with fewer requests than the minimum says nothing yet, so the rule is to hold at the stage.

options.text: Roll back to zero, since too few requests counts as a failed stage
options.says: Ruled out because the share goes back to zero only when errors pass the limit: "Over it, the share goes back to zero".

options.text: Declare the roll-out complete, since no error has been seen so far
options.says: Ruled out because a roll-out ends with "One stage up, and `complete` at 100 percent".

questions.stem: A staged roll-out is at 25 percent of requests when the error rate passes its limit. What happens next?

options.text: Drop to 5 percent and keep the roll-out running, to gather more evidence from a smaller share
options.says: Ruled out because "Reducing to a smaller share keeps part of the damage on the path".

options.text: Hold at 25 percent and investigate, leaving those customers on the new model while the errors continue to arrive
options.says: Ruled out because "Holding at the stage while errors continue leaves the share of customers who see them where it is".

options.text: Advance to 100 percent so that the failure shows up clearly in the data of the whole base
options.says: Ruled out because "Advancing to 100 percent to see the failure in the full data makes every customer the sample".

options.text: Send all traffic back to the previous model, which stays available until its own retirement
options.says: The limit is passed, so the share goes back to zero and the previous model, still configured, takes the traffic.
